messages: Maria (Product Designer): quick design check — roles matrix with 8+ roles is feeling pretty dense on smaller screens. also the SSO enforcement toggle in the invite drawer is getting missed in usability tests. thinking through three options: A) collapse rows with a lightweight 'show details' chevron, B) keep full rows but add inline search + persistent keyboard focus ring, C) move SSO toggle to top-level org security header and make it sticky. also: audit log 'view' currently opens a modal that traps focus (QA flagged). thoughts? :thinking_face: TJ (Frontend): i ran perf on collapse vs full rows — collapse is cheaper for paint but adds more DOM toggles. keyboard focus is doable either way. for collapse, we'll need proper aria-expanded + focus management. example pattern: TJ (Frontend): ```html ...detail cells... ``` Ash (PM): my leaning is B (inline search + focus) — smaller dev lift, less UX churn. we can A as an accessibility-first follow-up if needed. can we do quick AB: 10% of orgs see B vs A and measure time-to-find SSO + invite completion? Sam (UX Research): in our unmoderated tests, 6/10 participants failed to find SSO enforcement when it was nested in the drawer. when it's surfaced on the top security header, discovery jumps to 9/10. people mentally group SSO with org-level security controls. Lee (Accessibility): important notes: - modal currently traps focus and doesn't return focus to the invoking control on close — BUG. - color contrast on role status pills (green/blue on light gray) falls below 4.5:1 for small text. - if we do collapse, make the toggle a real button, not a div, and use aria-expanded + aria-controls. roving tabindex for rows is preferred when rows are selectable. Lee (Accessibility): keyboard example snippet: Lee (Accessibility): ```html Role name ``` TJ (Frontend): +1 on returning focus from modal. easy fix. also for pill contrast we can add a stronger border or use a darker tone for text. cost is small. Ash (PM): ok action plan proposal: 1) ship B as low-risk (inline search, keyboard focus styles) behind a flag; 2) fix modal focus trap immediately (bugfix); 3) run a 2-week canary measuring invite completion + time-to-find SSO; 4) if metrics not good, prototype A (collapsible rows) with aria patterns. Maria (Product Designer): sounds good. i'll update the figma with the inline search and focus ring states and annotate ARIA roles. link: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/roles-grid-compactness (please comment) :slightly_smiling_face: audit-bot: BUG-4321 created: audit log modal focus trap. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BUG-4321 Sam (UX Research): i'll schedule a quick remote test for the canary cohort next week and add a short task to validate pill contrast with colorblind simulations. Lee (Accessibility): small nit: ensure the SSO toggle has an aria-describedby pointing to the short help text — users with screen readers need the enforcement implications explained. e.g. aria-describedby="sso-help-1". TJ (Frontend): i'll pick up the modal fix + aria-describedby for the toggle. estimate 1 day for modal + 2 days for inline search + focus ring polish. Ash (PM): assigning: TJ -> modal fix + toggle aria, Maria -> figma updates & copy, Sam -> canary test, Lee -> accessibility review, Maria/TJ -> implementation flag + rollout plan. target: patch + canary by EOW. :rocket: Maria (Product Designer): thanks. i'll push updated copy for the SSO help text: "When enforced, SSO requires all users to sign in with your organization's identity provider. This cannot be undone without admin action." — please review for tone. Lee (Accessibility): that copy looks clear. maybe add a short sentence for screen readers: "Learn more about SSO enforcement in the docs (link)." ensure link has descriptive text. TJ (Frontend): noted. i'll ping here when the modal fix is merged. :white_check_mark: Maria (Product Designer): closing loop — follow-ups in the PR and we can reconvene after the canary metrics. thanks everyone! :clap:
